newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay says mistery disease killing cattle.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay says mistery disease killing cattle.

text.p: A mystery disease is attacking Paraguayan cattle, the Agriculture and Livestock Ministry said Wednesday.
The disease is killing cattle near the town of Carapegua, 55 miles (90 km) south of the capital Asuncion, which is one of the main producing zones for beef for the local market.
The government still does not know how many animals have died, but local ranchers said they have suffered important losses.
One small cattle raiser, Juan Carlos Gonzalez, described how the affected animals die after a long agony.
"They lie down and three days later they begin to swell up until they die," Gonzalez told Reuters.
The governemnt's National Animal Health Service said that the disease could turn out to be a form of cattle rabies or else botulism.
But the service's director, Carlos Trapani, said that some of the symptoms do not match those diseases. Trapani said the definitive diagnosis should be known in the next few days.
An outbreak of cattle rabies killed 2,000 head in the zone of Neembucu, 200 miles (300 km) south of Asuncion in June.
